::: {#exm-perplexity-loaded-die}
#### Perplexity of a loaded die

<!-- no-figure: the example is a single number -->

Let $X$ be the roll of the loaded die from @exm-rarity-die,
where a six has [probability](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-probability) $1/2$
and each other face has probability $1/10$.
The code computes the [perplexity](#def-perplexity) from the [entropy](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-entropy) in [bits](#def-bit),
and then from the [rarities](#def-rarity) by @thm-perplexity-geometric-mean.

```{r}
#| label: perplexity-loaded-die
p_other_faces <- rep(1 / 10, 5)
p <- c(1 / 2, p_other_faces)
surprisal <- -log2(p)
entropy <- sum(p * surprisal)
perplexity_from_entropy <- 2^entropy
rarity <- 1 / p
perplexity_from_rarities <- prod(rarity^p)
c(perplexity_from_entropy, perplexity_from_rarities)
```

Both routes give a perplexity of about $`r round(perplexity_from_entropy, 2)`$.
The loaded die has the same entropy as a fair die with about that many faces,
fewer than the $6$ faces it has.

:::
